design.context: Real ChecksApplication only, no RuntimeHooks, mock, new browser/server framework, or synthetic revision; same PostgreSQL, catalog, policies, Core fixture and ordinary runner/token. Ephemeral production servlet required by worker HttpSecurity configuration; management port disabled to avoid another server. Reuse original DynamicPropertySource through its DynamicPropertyRegistry lambda, then override only worker lifetime/scheduling values; no duplicate fixture authority settings. Guided authoring enabled remains original true, also the prior default; worker HTTP security still denies public paths and no scheduled authoring task runs.
design.schedulers: Local initializer installs a normal BeanFactoryPostProcessor removing only standard scheduled-annotation processor after configuration parsing and before singleton postprocessing. Assert it absent. Disable producer/dispatcher/retry/partition/retention/report flags. Retain actual domain beans. SchedulingCoordinator owns idle targets until explicit stop/context destruction; no tick registered. PartitionBootstrap idempotent startup and CheckSourceMetrics gauges remain.
design.identity_assertions: test+worker active profiles; exact production StudioDispatcher and HttpRunnerDispatchClient; native ObservedRevisionVerifier installed by identity into actual readiness service and ObservedReplayAuthorization; dispatcher holds that authorization/client; readiness of genuinely published revision is true. Existing main context is not worker. Explicit !worker StudioController, StudioInternalController and GuidedPublicationController beans absent; callback token configured equal to original fixture.
design.route_proof: Second API execute accepted202 -> actual worker dispatcher -> exact actual HTTP client observed branch /v2/runs -> only production submitObserved router -> AdmissionCasService observed receipt -> existing PASSED/fresh-value assertions. No wire tap, script modification or body retention.
design.cleanup: Worker-only postprocessor recognizes exactly three AsyncConfig adapter bean names. Each real delegate is registered as its owning bean disposal callback before startup can fail. Callback shuts down, uses existing bounded-await helper, and increments a primitive counter only after confirmed termination. TaskExecutorAdapter installed public API has no close/shutdown and AsyncConfig declares no destroy method, so no existing disposal is overwritten. Spring context destruction executes all callbacks on normal close or startup failure; normal finally asserts inactive context and three confirmed disposals. Original startup exception remains unchanged.
design.logging: Worker Spring boot uses existing WARN test setting and can initialize global logging like existing historicalReplica boots. It is created/closed only in first nonsecret method. Original secret C5 independently attaches its own full ROOT+APP TRACE afterward and final checks verify both effective levels; its body/capture/scripts unchanged.
design.callback_authority: Production dispatcher/job has no callback destination/token fields. Existing ordinary runner owns both and still reports to original API context; worker send SERVICE bearer unchanged. Explicit CALLBACK setting parity does not redirect callbacks.

alternatives.tradeoff: One real worker context boot adds bounded integration cost but fulfills original missing profile obligation without another browser flow or matrix.

alternatives.rejected: Duplicates setup and cannot prove the actually published current revision lineage.
Unconditional metrics/coordinator scheduled tasks remain; pre-refresh standard scheduling processor removal is smaller and deterministic.
Unneeded because actual client/router and immutable observed admission receipt prove route; avoids new payload retention surfaces.

qualification: No production behavior, budgets, logging scope, fresh authority, all30 canary/privacy checks, or mandatory test count changes. Source checks cannot award runtime AC16; root must run existing pair after exact peer GO and strict helper checks.
independent_design: Runtime peer GO including exact three named disposal callbacks, exclusive /v2 route lineage and pre-acceptance context boot.
